Section 03 — what we are

A creative house,
not a hostel

Casa Kayam started from a simple idea: to create a place where the journey isn't just a stopover. A place where musicians, artists, travelers, and locals could meet around creation.

On a finca surrounded by nature, two kilometers from the village, you'll find a hostel, a professional recording studio, and a community that changes every week.

Section 07 — Location

Two kilometers

from the village.

A thousand
from mass tourism

While Guatapé welcomes thousands of visitors every day, Casa Kayam offers a quiet retreat: nature, silence, views over the embalse. When you want to go into the village, the moto-chiva takes you there in 5 minutes for 10,000 COP. Or you walk — 25 minutes down the road.

Section 09 — Before you book

Frequently asked

questions .

From Medellín's Terminal del Norte, take a bus to Guatapé (about 2 hours, 25,000 COP). Buses run frequently. Once in Guatapé, a moto-chiva will bring you to Casa Kayam for 10,000 COP — every driver in town knows us. If you prefer to walk, it's a 25-minute walk down the road from the village.

Yes. Many of our long-stay guests are digital nomads who work from the coworking space or from the terrace. WiFi reaches all common areas and most rooms. Coworking is included in private rooms, Mapalé, and glamping.

We're 2 kilometers from the center of Guatapé. The moto-chiva takes 5 minutes for 10,000 COP, walking takes about 25 minutes. Many of our guests appreciate the distance — it means real silence, nature, and views over the embalse.

Yes. We have two fully equipped kitchens — one for guests and one for volunteers. There's a small village shop nearby, and the village center has supermarkets and fresh markets.

Some are free — yoga, jam sessions, bonfires, film screenings, sports tournaments. Others are paid — recording studio sessions, production classes, art workshops, vocal coaching. You'll find the weekly program at reception and on our community WhatsApp group.

Both, depending on the night. We host jam sessions, concerts, and gatherings — but we're a cultural center, not a party hostel. Common areas wind down by 11 PM, and we respect the rhythm of those who came here to rest, work, or create.

Yes. We have private rooms suitable for families and can accommodate groups of various sizes. For specific arrangements, write to us on WhatsApp — we'll find the best setup for you.

Absolutely. Kayam Records is open to professionals and to those just starting out. We offer recording sessions, vocal coaching, production classes, and DJ lessons — at every level. Just let us know what you're looking for.

Travel details

How to get there from Medellin

1.

How to get to Terminal del Norte

By Metro: Take Line A (blue) of the Medellin Metro and get off at Caribe station. From there, there is a direct pedestrian bridge connecting to the bus terminal.

2.

Where to buy tickets

Inside the terminal, go to the ticket counters operated by the authorized companies for this route:

Counter 14: Operated by Sotrasanvicente.

Counters 9 or 8: Operated by Sotrapenol.

3.

Schedules and Frequency

First bus: 5:30 a.m.

Frequency: Buses leave approximately every 30 to 60 minutes.

Last bus: Around 6:30 p.m. or 7:00 p.m. depending on the company.
